reuse.why: The change reuses the existing category eligibility predicate, amount conversion, tag extraction, budget writes, batching, and undo registration.

duplication.why: Eligibility and sign conversion remain shared across consumers, with only action-specific orchestration and data retrieval repeated.

placement.why: Category policy and budget operations remain in budget/actions.ts, tag parsing stays shared, and method registration stays in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The edits are limited to the requested month-wide policies, new spending action, method registration, and related tests.

maintainability.why: The shared policy remains straightforward, although using the 'average' discriminator for last-month spending makes its eligibility semantics less explicit.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All affected month-wide actions use isWrittenByMonthAction, and setLastMonthSpending also uses toAverageBudgetAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The new consumer calls the existing policy and conversion helpers rather than reshaping their logic locally.

abstraction_drift.where: isWrittenByMonthAction gains the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter and shared exclusions without adding consumer-specific branches or bypasses.
